description:
Parent: op-841p. Maintainer requirement 2026-08-11: the pipeline must be REPRODUCIBLE by someone else on another machine. This is a design constraint on the architecture, not a bolt-on - it changes what each stage writes to disk.

WHAT REPRODUCIBLE MUST MEAN HERE:
1. Every stage re-runnable from committed inputs WITHOUT re-running the stage above. Each hand-off is a real on-disk artefact with its own provenance, not an in-memory value. The MGXS library in particular must be a file a human can inspect and diff.
2. A MANIFEST PER RUN recording: workspace git commit; cross-section library and version (e.g. ENDF/B-VIII.0 and the exact tape); fidelity tier (from_core LOW vs from_endf HIGH); MC RNG seed, particles per generation, inactive and active generation counts; group structure; homogenisation choice; mesh and its generation parameters; and the code path taken at each rung. A result whose data version is unknown is not reproducible.
3. Deterministic given a seed. run_keff_delta_seq is already documented as the bit-reproducible reference (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/keff_delta.rs:285-295) and the rayon backend is thread-count-invariant by seed jump-ahead (:382-393). Report sigma with every MC number.
4. Scriptable, not interactive - which is what makes rung-to-rung validation automatable in CI.
5. Intermediate artefacts ARE the validation evidence. A pcm comparison between rungs means nothing if the artefacts it came from are gone.

HEADLESS ENTRY POINT: a function taking a geometry description plus a run configuration, so outram-blender can drive it as a third solver bridge (op-hzs.53). Do NOT make it test-only.

WHERE IT GOES: crates/nee_soon is the designated coupling layer (op-fr2) and its xin_wang_sp3_workflow scaffold (src/xin_wang_sp3_workflow/, 828 lines, self-declared 'scaffold only' at mod.rs:26) is already the right SHAPE - a four-stage njoy -> mc -> genfoam chain. But today nee_soon exposes exactly one real method, NeeSoon::new_prompt_excursion_model (src/lib.rs:111-131), a pass-through to Nordheim-Fuchs. There is no headless pipeline entry point anywhere in the workspace yet.

CAVEAT TO CARRY: rung 1 reproducibility is compromised until op-rbo and op-jis close. Per crates/outram-mc-libs/CLAUDE.md (maintainer decision 2026-08-06) bit-for-bit parity with OpenMC is explicitly NOT required - statistical correctness and stream separation are. Frame the manifest requirement on that standard.
title: HTR-10 pipeline: reproducibility manifest and headless scriptable entry point

description:
s4 and s37. Create .git/ and write the generated .gitignore on Create Kovan Folder, so a non-Git user gets a valid repo without learning Git (s46 'Create library' acceptance scenario). .gitignore must at minimum carry: /.kovan/, /literature/proprietary/pdf/, *.tmp, *.swp, *~. Restricted PDFs must NEVER be capable of entering Save Repository.

NOT A NEW DEPENDENCY -- gix is already in the tree. Root Cargo.toml:172 pins gix = "0.85", default-features = false, features [sha1, revision, status, blame, dirwalk, index], consumed read-only by kovan-discovery. This step needs write/init/commit features ADDED.

*** YANKED-DEPENDENCY HAZARD, verified 2026-08-31. Do NOT bump gix to 0.86. *** gix 0.86 pins gix-protocol ^0.64.0, and gix-protocol 0.64.0/0.65.0 depend on bisync ^0.3.0 -- EVERY published bisync (0.1.0, 0.2.0-0.2.3, 0.3.0, 0.3.1) is yanked on crates.io, so a fresh resolve dead-ends with 'failed to select a version for the requirement bisync = ^0.3.0'. This workspace is currently SAFE only because gix 0.85 resolves gix-protocol to 0.63.0, which predates the bisync dependency (confirmed: bisync absent from Cargo.lock; a lock-deleted `cargo generate-lockfile` succeeds, exit 0, 959 packages). If this step bumps gix at all, the safe target is 0.87.1 -- the first gix requiring gix-protocol 0.65.1, which dropped bisync. Same wall kopi-beans 0.1.9 hit and fixed (kopitiam clone c016c8b, 2026-08-31). Per the dependency policy, edit the ROOT Cargo.toml only.
title: kovan redesign 04: gitoxide init + generated .gitignore (gix write features)

description:
The second HTGR-specific accident sequence. HTR-10 has a once-through helical-coil steam generator with helium on the shell side at 3.0 MPa and water/steam in the tubes at 4.0 MPa, so the water side is at HIGHER pressure than the helium. A tube rupture therefore drives water into the primary circuit, not the other way round.

THE PHYSICS. Steam meets hot graphite: C + H2O -> CO + H2 (the steam-graphite reaction, endothermic), followed by the WATER-GAS SHIFT reaction CO + H2O <-> CO2 + H2. Consequences: graphite corrosion, hydrogen generation, and a moderator/reactivity effect from the water in the core. The shift reaction is equilibrium-limited and strongly temperature dependent, which is exactly what a Gibbs minimiser is for.

THE PAYOFF THE MAINTAINER IDENTIFIED. This is the same chemistry as the refinery epic op-1z3o. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/reactors/gibbs_reactor.rs serves both, and DWSIM SHIPS TWO WATER-GAS SHIFT REFERENCE FLOWSHEETS that are converged cases with known answers:
  PlatformFiles/Common/tests/WATER_GAS_SHIFT_REACTION.dwxmz
  PlatformFiles/Common/tests/Flowsheet5_StudyOnTheEffectsOfInertsOnWaterGasShiftReaction.dwxmz
in the pinned upstream clone at /home/teddy0/Documents/research/dwsim-upstream (branch windows, commit 1abf72d1b6b41d3e9a8cc770d3cc4e8fc76e5766, GPL-3.0). Those are ready-made V&V cases for the shift chemistry, and validating the reactor block once serves BOTH the refinery hydrogen plant and this accident sequence.

So: validate the shift reactor against the DWSIM reference flowsheets first, then apply it to the graphite-steam system. Do not build a second, separate shift implementation.
title: HTR-10 accident: water/steam ingress and the water-gas shift reaction
